about.title: About us
about.intro: At Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional, we work to support, guide, and strengthen Ecuadorian and Latin American communities in New York while sustaining the cultural and human bonds that bring us together.
about.seoDescription: Learn about the mission, values, and projects of Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional, an organization supporting Ecuadorian and Latin American communities in New York.
about.heroTitle: United by our roots. Driven by our community.
about.heroDescription: At Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional, we work to support, guide, and strengthen Ecuadorian and Latin American communities in New York while sustaining the cultural and human bonds that bring us together.
about.teamPhotoAlt: AEINY community members gathered together around a table.
about.teamPhotoCaption: A community connected by shared roots and care
about.identityTitle: Our roots unite us. Our community moves us forward.
about.identityCopy1: Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional (AEI) is a community organization based in New York, committed to the well-being and development of Ecuadorian and Latin American communities.
about.identityCopy2: Through educational programs, community guidance, cultural activities, and institutional collaboration, we seek to create opportunities and strengthen ties between migrants, their families, and their communities of origin.
about.identityCopy3: Our work connects the needs of people building a life in the United States with recognition of their roots, identity, and contributions to society.
about.storyPhotoAlt: AEINY volunteers and community members gathered with donated food and supplies.
about.missionHeading: A shared purpose, a vision for the future.
about.missionPhotoAlt: AEINY volunteers sharing essential supplies with community members.
about.missionCopy: To support and strengthen Ecuadorian and Latin American communities through access to information, education, guidance, and development opportunities, while encouraging community participation, dignity, and solidarity.
about.visionCopy: An informed, connected, and empowered migrant community with opportunities to thrive and maintain strong ties to its cultural identity and roots.

about.rootsPhotoCaption: A shared celebration of Ecuadorian and Latin American identity.

value.solidarityCopy: We believe in mutual support and in the strength of a community that moves forward together.
value.identityCopy: We value our roots and foster connection across generations and cultures.
value.educationCopy: We see knowledge and learning as tools for opening new opportunities.
value.commitmentCopy: We work to strengthen participation, collaboration, and collective well-being.

about.centerLead: A place for learning, guidance, and connection for New York's migrant community.
about.centerCopy: Through educational and community initiatives, Centro Comunitario Andino shares information about construction-industry training, cultural identity, immigration matters, workplace issues, and human rights.
about.parkTitle: A tribute to those who build bridges between countries.
about.parkCopy1: Parque del Migrante, advanced in collaboration with the Municipality of Cuenca, Ecuador, is an initiative dedicated to recognizing the efforts, sacrifices, and contributions of Ecuadorian migrants.
about.parkCopy2: The project represents the connection between communities of origin and those who have built new opportunities far from home.
about.finalTitle: When a community comes together, opportunities grow.
about.finalDescription: Your involvement can help strengthen educational, cultural, and community initiatives that make a difference.

ourWork.title: Our Work
ourWork.intro: Our initiatives connect people, families, and institutions around migration, education, cultural practice, and community wellness.
ourWork.seoDescription: Discover how Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional supports immigrant families and workers through education, community resources, cultural identity and advocacy.
ourWork.heroIntro: Alianza Ecuatoriana Internacional works alongside immigrant families, workers and communities to expand access to education, practical support, cultural connection and opportunities to build a stronger future.
ourWork.heroPhotoAlt: AEINY volunteers sharing essential supplies with community members.
ourWork.pillarsIntro: Our work grows from the everyday needs of the community — from education and workplace preparation to immigrant guidance, cultural identity and the defense of dignity and rights.

area.educationCopy: We help community members gain practical knowledge and skills that can open doors to safer work and greater economic opportunity. Through Centro Comunitario Andino, programs include construction-related education and workplace safety training.
area.supportCopy: For immigrants building a new life in the United States, reliable information matters. AEINY connects community members with guidance related to immigration, work, local resources and everyday challenges.
area.rightsCopy: AEINY's community work is rooted in the belief that immigrants and workers deserve information, respect and the ability to understand and defend their rights.
area.cultureCopy: Keeping culture alive is also a form of community building. Through gatherings, traditions and cultural initiatives, AEINY creates spaces where Ecuadorian identity can be shared across generations and with the wider Latino community.

festival2026.seoTitle: International Andean Film Festival 2026 | Kuri Chasqui Awards | AEINY
festival2026.seoDescription: Discover the 1st International Andean Film Festival in New York and the Kuri Chasqui Awards, celebrating Andean cinema, culture, identity and audiovisual storytelling.
festival2026.title: 1st International Andean Film Festival
festival2026.heroIntro: A celebration of Andean cinema, cultural identity, migration, memory and the voices connecting the Andes with the world.
festival2026.heroImageAlt: Community members taking part in a cultural parade.
festival2026.heroImageCaption: Culture and community, at the heart of AEINY.
festival2026.aboutAside: An AEINY cultural initiative connecting filmmakers, artists and communities across countries.
festival2026.aboutCopy: Founded and directed by Walther Sinche and Amaruk Kayshapanta, the International Andean Film Festival is a cultural platform dedicated to audiovisual works related to Andean cultures, identity, migration, human rights, memory and contemporary social realities.
festival2026.awardsCopy: “Kuri Chasqui” is a Kichwa / Quechua expression translated by the organizers as “The Golden Messenger.” The awards recognize outstanding audiovisual professionals and works connected with Andean cinema and culture.
festival2026.awardsContext: The name draws on Andean cosmovision, ancestral philosophy and the cultures of Tawantinsuyu and South America. The awards are planned as annual international Andean film awards beginning in 2026.
festival2026.awardRecognition: A symbol of transmitting knowledge, culture, memory and Andean worldview.

kuri2026Page.seoTitle: Kuri Chasqui 2026 | The Andes International Film Fest New York | AEINY
kuri2026Page.seoDescription: Discover Kuri Chasqui 2026, The Andes International Film Fest New York, celebrating Andean cinema, identity, memory and culture in New York from November 8–15, 2026.
kuri2026Page.heroSubtitle: The Andes International Film Fest New York
kuri2026Page.heroSupporting: Andean cinema arrives in the heart of New York.
kuri2026Page.posterAlt: Official poster for Kuri Chasqui 2026, The Andes International Film Fest New York.
kuri2026Page.aboutTitle: Stories, memory and identity of the Andes—on screen in New York.
kuri2026Page.aboutCopy: Kuri Chasqui is a cultural platform created to bring the stories, memory and identity of the Andes to New York through cinema. Born from the intersection of social activism, Indigenous identity and artistic expression, the festival creates a space where the Andean diaspora can reconnect with its roots while sharing its stories with a wider audience.
kuri2026Page.whyTitle: Why Andean cinema matters in New York
kuri2026Page.whyCopyOne: For migrant communities from Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and Colombia in New York, Andean cinema can be a direct connection to home. It gives visibility to Indigenous and rural cultures, and helps preserve stories, memory and language across generations.
kuri2026Page.whyCopyTwo: Many Andean productions incorporate Indigenous languages such as Kichwa and Aimara. Hearing these languages in a New York cinema gives them public space and can help younger generations stay connected to their heritage.
kuri2026Page.rootsDescription: Connecting diaspora communities with their cultural heritage.
kuri2026Page.visibilityDescription: Giving space to Indigenous, rural and Andean identities.
kuri2026Page.memoryDescription: Using cinema as a living archive of migration, history and language.
kuri2026Page.connectionDescription: Bringing filmmakers, communities and audiences together in New York.
kuri2026Page.editionTitle: Andean stories, shared in New York.
kuri2026Page.editionCopy: The planned programming brings together community cinema, documentaries about migrant memory and award-winning feature films from the region.
kuri2026Page.programTitle: Eight days of cinema and community.
kuri2026Page.awardCopy: The Kuri Chasqui statuette is the official distinction awarded to festival winners. Designed specifically for this event, it brings together pre-Columbian heritage and the contemporary artistic experience of the Andean diaspora.
